requirements.requirement: Provide at least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap on node1.
requirements.summary: The active /dev/zram0 device is identified as zram using lzo compression, has a 536,870,912-byte disk size, and is mounted as swap.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the compressed swap activates automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: A bounded reboot changed the boot identity, after which zram-swap.service was enabled and active and /dev/zram0 had recovered as active swap. The fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot change.

requirements.requirement: Prefer the in-memory swap over any disk-backed swap.
requirements.summary: /dev/zram0 is active at the maximum Linux swap priority of 32767, and the post-reboot validation found no other swap with equal or higher priority.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a boot-persistent, lzo-compressed 512 MiB zram swap device at priority 32767, and its successful recovery was directly demonstrated across a reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the matching kernel module package, loading zram, creating and enabling its service, and rebooting all had clear roles in implementing or validating the required boot-persistent swap. Temporary apt coordination files did not remain after reboot. Final observations show healthy package state, no failed services, and no new listening sockets.
